text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "The SchNet passage says its C20 force field was trained on reference data from DFT (PBE+vdW-TS) calculations [W2778051509#019]. The DiffTRe authors see the main obstacle to this bottom-up learning as the limited availability of highly precise and sufficiently broad data sets. For larger systems such as macromolecules, quantum mechanics computations will stay intractable, which prevents ab initio data set generation altogether [W3168247670#003]. Instead, DiffTRe takes a top-down approach and trains neural network potentials on experimental data. The test cases are DimeNet++ for diamond, trained on its experimental stiffness tensor, and DimeNet++ for coarse-grained water, trained on pressure and on radial and angular distribution functions [W3168247670#003]."}
